subject: Query: March marketplace invoice proration & withholding
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sinha <priya@acmecloud.com>, Acme Cloud Marketplace Billing <billing@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Query: March marketplace invoice proration & withholding

Hi Priya / Acme billing team,

We ran our month-end reconciliation and noticed two items on the March marketplace invoice that don't align with the usage files:

1) A prorated charge on 2027-03-05 for $4,312 labelled "proration adjustment" that doesn't appear in our metering export.
2) A 6% tax withholding line labelled "EU Withholding" for $2,750 — our contract with Acme (Marketplace Terms, section 7) does not call for withholding on payouts.

Can you share the raw metering rows that generated the proration and the tax code you applied? Marcus and Neha are looped in for reconciliation. If this is an unapplied credit or vendor withholding, we need the ledger entry + invoice-level justification so we can present to Finance before the payout cutoff next Wednesday.

Attachments: none on our side in this message.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Priya Sinha <priya@acmecloud.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Farrell <john.farrell@acmecloud.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Query: March marketplace invoice proration & withholding

Hi Laura — thanks for flagging. Apologies for the noise. We've attached the metering export and the invoice pdf for March so you can see the native rows. Short answers up front:

- The "proration adjustment" is a system-level correction applied when a SKU rate changed mid-billing-cycle; it is calculated from prorating the delta in per-unit price for a small set of SKUs that were migrated on 2027-03-04. The meter rows are in acme_metering_export_Mar2027.csv (column "reason" = PRORATE_ADJ).
- The 6% withholding was applied automatically by our EU tax module when the seller entity was flagged for "local_withholding_required". That flag was set during onboarding and looks to be stale; we'll remove it if you confirm your tax docs.

We've attached: acme_metering_export_Mar2027.csv and acme_invoice_Mar2027.pdf. Also sharing an internal note (not an attachment) that the tax flag came from a legacy onboarding form.

If you can confirm the seller entity tax ID and forward the W-8/W-9 or local tax certs for the EU entity, we can reprocess the withholding and issue an adjustment credit prior to the next settlement.

Best,
Priya
Priya Sinha
Marketplace Billing Lead
Acme Cloud Marketplace
priya@acmecloud.com

Subject: Re: Query: March marketplace invoice proration & withholding

Thanks, Priya — that helps. A few follow-ups from our side after an initial pass through the CSV and invoice: 

- The PRORATE_ADJ rows in the export show line_items for sku vm.large-io between 2027-03-04T22:00Z and 2027-03-05T02:00Z. However, internal tag mapping indicates those were billed under an old SKU (vm.large). Marcus: can you confirm if the migration mapping was meant to preserve rate parity? If not, we need a breakdown that shows unit counts × old_rate vs new_rate.

- On withholding: our legal/tax team confirms Redwood is a US-based seller with valid tax docs on file in your onboarding portal (EIN: 12-3456789). We did not opt into local EU withholding. Please mark the seller entity as "no_local_withholding" and re-run the payout calculation.

We've attached our internal reconciliation workbook (redwood_internal_recon_Mar2027.xlsx) with a suggested credit amount of $6,987 (proration reversal + withheld amount) and the line mapping. If Acme can issue a one-line adjustment credit against invoice #ACME-INV-2027-03, we can accept that and move forward with the scheduled payout.

Next steps requested:
- Priya / John: confirm the mapping and whether Acme will credit or issue an invoice correction by 2027-03-31.
- Marcus: quick validation of SKU mapping and counts.

Appreciate the quick turnaround on this — payout cutoff is end of day next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Laura
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Sinha <priya@acmecloud.com>

Subject: Re: Query: March marketplace invoice proration & withholding

Laura / Marcus / Neha — quick update. I confirmed with our metering ops and tax team: 

1) SKU mapping: the rate change was intended to be rate-neutral for existing sellers but a translation bug caused a temporary delta. We've extracted the unit-level math and attached adjustment_credit_2027-03-29.pdf that reflects the reversal. Total credit issued: $4,237 (slightly different from your calc after rounding policy).

2) Withholding: we removed the "local_withholding_required" flag for Redwood's seller entity and reprocessed the withholding. We issued a withholding reversal credit of $2,750 and will re-run the payout.

3) Payout timing: adjustments will be reflected in the next settlement window; the net effect is a single one-line credit against invoice ACME-INV-2027-03. We also added an internal ticket to prevent the onboarding flag from reactivating.

Attachments: adjustment_credit_2027-03-29.pdf

I'll also send a small reconciliation csv to the accounting alias if you want a ledger-friendly export. Let me know if the final credit amounts need additional doc support for Redwood Finance.

Thanks — and sorry again for the churn.

Best,
Priya
Marketplace Billing Lead
Acme Cloud Marketplace
